title: Digit Decodings
statement:
Count the ways a digit string can be read as letters.

Contract
- Each letter is encoded by a number: `1` is A, `2` is B, ..., `26` is Z. A string of digits is decoded by splitting it into consecutive pieces, each of which is one of the numbers `1`..`26` written without leading zeros (so `0` and `06` are not valid pieces).
- `digits` is a non-null string made only of the characters `0`-`9`, with at most 1,000,000 characters. Return the number of different splits, modulo 1,000,000,007, as an `int`.
- The empty string and any string with no valid split give `0`.

Examples
- `count("12")` returns `2` (`1|2` and `12`).
- `count("226")` returns `3` (`2|2|6`, `22|6`, `2|26`).
- `count("06")` returns `0`.
hints: Look at the end of the string: the last piece is either one digit or two digits. Which of those are legal?

The number of splits of a prefix is the sum of the counts for the prefix one shorter (if the last digit is not 0) and two shorter (if the last two digits form 10..26). Only the last two counts are ever needed.
Keep two rolling counts and reduce modulo 1,000,000,007 at every step. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the string length.
inputSyntax: Input: a string of digits, for example: 226
